# database schema mechanics

open splunk embeds an ordered migration history for each database. every
history starts with exactly one complete `0001_baseline.sql`; later schema
changes are appended as contiguous, immutable versioned scripts. a fresh
database applies the baseline and every forward migration, while a database
whose verified ledger is an exact prefix applies only the pending suffix.

forward upgrades from a shipped migration prefix are supported. downgrades,
gapped or rewritten histories, unledgered schema adoption, and migration from
an unrelated source history are not.

migration sequence numbers, ledger digests, entity/catalog revisions, and
private row-format counters are implementation mechanics. they detect drift,
stale writes, and unrecognized local state; they are not product versions or
public compatibility levels.

## ledger contract

migration files are embedded into the server. filenames carry contiguous
four-digit versions, beginning with `0001_baseline.sql`. before applying a
pending script, the runner validates every existing ledger row's version,
name, and sha-256 digest against the corresponding embedded file. missing,
renamed, modified, duplicated, gapped, or unexpected rows fail as drift.
successful scripts are recorded once, so reopening and retrying the current
history is safe. tests pin every shipped migration's sha-256 digest: an applied
script is never edited or replaced; a schema change requires a newly appended
migration.

one released sqlite baseline folded the ingest write-group schema into version
`0001` after the original baseline had shipped. the runner narrowly recognizes
that exact alternate checksum, adopts the corresponding accounting migration,
and then rejoins the canonical history. no other alternate checksum or
rewritten migration is accepted. pre-accounting pending reservations retain
their original outbox and are replayed individually before new write groups are
formed.

the principal-backlog migration preserves every accepted reservation and adds
an immutable server-derived source identity for new admission. older rows keep
an empty identity; their pending rows and bytes count conservatively against
every principal until replay makes them terminal. token retirement never
deletes backlog accounting, and recovery does not reassign accepted work.

an unrecognized ledger or unledgered legacy schema is not silently adopted,
rewritten, or deleted. provision a fresh database or volume and retain old state
separately if forensic access is required.

sqlite validates and applies all pending migrations transactionally under one
startup writer lock. clickhouse ddl is not transactional, so each clickhouse
migration must use retry-safe ddl and write its ledger row last. gorm never
runs `automigrate`.

## sqlite control plane

sqlite is the authority for catalogs, optimistic-concurrency revisions,
authentication/token metadata, collectors, jobs/history/export,
saved searches, dashboards, knowledge/lookups, visibility, quota schedules,
ingestion request/outbox state, audit journals (including the identity-free
feature-operation journal), cursors, and recovery metadata.

audited business mutations and their audit/receipt/catalog changes share one
caller-owned transaction. the schema uses explicit foreign keys, uniqueness,
bounds, state transitions, and immutable-row triggers so malformed state fails
at the storage boundary and again during hydration.

sqlite and the server master-key/administrator-token files are one control-
plane recovery unit. do not copy a live database independently of the
coordinated recovery procedure in [`deploy/readme.md`](../deploy/readme.md).

## clickhouse event store

one `open_splunk.events` table stores all logical indexes. tenant and index lead
the sort/primary key, followed by bounded time and stable identity components.
monthly event-time partitions keep cardinality bounded. `event_time` preserves
nanoseconds, `index_time` records server admission, and `expires_at` stores the
index retention decision at admission. ttl removes expired rows in background
without relying on whole-part deletion across mixed index policies.

promoted columns represent canonical event metadata. optional promoted strings
remain nullable so missing and empty differ. dynamic `fields` uses the native
clickhouse json type with bounded dedicated paths/types; aligned `field_names`
and `field_types` preserve canonical dotted paths and stable logical value
types, including null and extended bytes/time/duration/decimal values. the
writer derives metadata and its private format discriminator from the original
typed protobuf value rather than inferring it later from physical json.

canonical spl aliases hide physical names: `index` maps to `index_name`,
`_time` to `event_time`, `_indextime` to `index_time`, `_raw` to `raw`, and
`message` to `body`. raw bytes use the native byte-safe insertion path; they
must not be utf-8-repaired or base64-replaced.

case-insensitive exact searches on `event_id`, `trace_id`, and `span_id` use
normalized bloom indexes that match the compiler's search expressions. the
forward migration adds index metadata without rewriting existing event parts
or changing their results. new parts build the indexes automatically. to
accelerate older parts immediately, a clickhouse administrator can schedule
the following maintenance separately from server startup:

```sql
alter table open_splunk.events materialize index idx_event_id_ci;
alter table open_splunk.events materialize index idx_trace_id_ci;
alter table open_splunk.events materialize index idx_span_id_ci;
```

materialization reads existing parts and runs asynchronously; its cost depends
on retained data volume. the application does not require materialization
privileges, and searches remain correct before it finishes.

## visibility, retries, and recovery

sqlite reserves a stable positive visibility sequence, index time, and
per-index retention snapshot before clickhouse insertion. successful insert
marks the reservation committed; a known pre-send failure may be skipped; an
ambiguous send retains the gap and identical outbox payload until
reconciliation proves its result.

search captures the highest contiguous committed sequence and one immutable
index-time cutoff. every event scan applies tenant/index/time authority plus
`index_time <= cutoff`, `expires_at > cutoff`, and
`visibility_seq <= committed_cutoff`. ttl expiry therefore cannot make the
logical visibility high-water move backward.

native collector and hec retries reuse deterministic event identities, row
order, settings, and source-revision-specific deduplication domains.
clickhouse's mergetree deduplication is a bounded recent-block window, not
global exactly-once delivery. an acknowledgment is issued only after commit
authority; ambiguous outcomes keep durable work pending.

sqlite and clickhouse form one coordinated recovery generation. a recovery
set binds their exact private schema/migration counters and digests. restore
never mixes a control plane from one generation with clickhouse from another.
unknown state fails closed; recovery does not discard it as success.

the sqlite half of that generation contains both logical ingestion
reservations and immutable write-group membership. a snapshot must therefore
never retain an ambiguous group without every referenced reservation outbox.
online backup, index deletion, and other physical maintenance use the shared
write freeze and drain proof before copying or mutating either store. terminal
group membership is pruned before referenced logical identity rows in the same
bounded maintenance transaction.

## verification

fast schema, final-shape, ordered-history, upgrade-preservation, ledger,
digest, drift, and retry tests run in the default suite. clickhouse smoke tests
reapply the current history, verify typed json/metadata and retry
deduplication, and use the repository-pinned image:

```sh
go test ./migrations/...

open_splunk_clickhouse_integration=1 \
go test ./migrations/clickhouse -run againstclickhouse -count=1 -v
```

set `open_splunk_clickhouse_test_image` only for an intentional pinned-image
comparison. a schema smoke pass does not replace ingestion, query, recovery,
load, or soak gates.

internal/hec/testdata/compatibility/readme.md
# hec protocol fixtures

these files are the machine-consumable examples for
[`docs/hec.md`](../../../../docs/hec.md). `fixture.schema.json` validates each corpus
document; the other json files are corpus documents.

fixture format discriminators are private test mechanics, not public hec or
release versions. the corpus covers only the exact unversioned routes described
by the current source contract; versioned aliases are unsupported.

each case is isolated. a harness creates exactly the declared token, indexes,
channel sequence, acknowledgment rows, and injected conditions, captures the
declared utc receive time, sends the request, then compares:

1. http status, selected headers, and `body_utf8` byte-for-byte;
2. the complete durable side-effect disposition;
3. normalized staged event projections; and
4. an optional spl query/result projection after reconciliation.

## placeholders

request header values may contain `{{token:<alias>}}`. the harness replaces it
with a fresh valid plaintext credential for the setup token with that alias.
`{{token:unknown}}` means a well-formed credential absent from the fixture
store. no checked-in fixture contains a usable secret. no other interpolation
is performed.

## body generators

- `utf8`: use `value` as its exact utf-8 bytes.
- `base64`: strict rfc 4648 decode of `value`.
- `gzip_utf8`: generate one gzip member containing `value`, with deterministic
  header fields (mtime zero, empty name/comment, os 255).
- `concatenated_gzip_utf8`: generate and concatenate one deterministic member
  for every string in `members`.
- `repeat_utf8`: repeat the exact utf-8 `unit` `count` times without building a
  checked-in multi-megabyte fixture.

the harness sets `content-length` from generated bytes unless a request header
explicitly supplies it.

## setup defaults and fault conditions

no undeclared token, index, channel, acknowledgment, quota debt, or outbox row
exists. optional token defaults are absent unless present in `defaults`.
indexes have no default sourcetype unless declared.

acknowledgment rows and scripted opaque allocations in setup are decimal
strings. emitted ids are positive integers no greater than `2^53-1`, so
javascript and other fixture consumers preserve them exactly. wire request and
response bodies remain exact json strings and contain json integer ids as
required by the protocol.

`conditions` are deterministic protected-boundary injections and do not bypass
earlier error precedence:

- `quota_limited` uses `retry_after_seconds`;
- `staging_busy` is transient admission unavailability;
- `staging_internal` is a permanent internal staging failure;
- `shutdown` closes the admission gate;
- `outbox_capacity` exhausts the durable hec work bound;
- `ack_capacity` exhausts the token/channel ack bound;
- `queue_unhealthy` and `ack_unhealthy` drive health projections.

## durable disposition vocabulary

- `absent`: no row/charge of that kind exists after the request;
- `staged`, `pending`, `reserved`, or `charged`: the successful request created
  the corresponding authority;
- `unchanged`: fixture prestate exists or may exist and the request did not
  mutate it.

event ids, request ids, source sequences, visibility numbers, index time, and
expiry are server-assigned and are intentionally omitted from event
projections. their invariants require implementation tests in addition to this
wire corpus.

## validation

from the repository root, syntax-check every json file with:

```sh
find internal/hec/testdata/compatibility -name '*.json' -print0 | xargs -0 -n1 jq empty
```

then run the dependency-free closed-schema and corpus invariant validator:

```sh
node internal/hec/testdata/compatibility/validate.mjs
```

when python `jsonschema` is available, validate corpus structure with:

```sh
python3 -m jsonschema -i internal/hec/testdata/compatibility/json-event.json internal/hec/testdata/compatibility/fixture.schema.json
```

repeat `-i` for each corpus document. a go fixture loader should validate the
same closed shape (or invoke a json schema validator) before executing cases.

nodes.text:
# Open Splunk Collector configuration.
#
# The daemon persists everything under state.directory:
#   <dir>/wal/            durable, fsync-on-append event-batch queue
#   <dir>/checkpoints/    per-file read offsets (advanced only after terminal delivery)
#   <dir>/dead-letter.jsonl  events the server permanently rejected
#   <dir>/collector_id    stable collector id, generated once and reused across restarts
#
# Before requesting an ingestion token, run `open-splunk-collector identity
# -config /etc/open-splunk/collector.yaml` with the final state directory
# mounted as a real collector-owned directory beneath a trusted parent. The
# token file may still be absent. Bind the issued token to the printed ID, then
# store its one-time plaintext value at server.token_file.
# Never copy or regenerate collector_id independently of the rest of the state.
#
# Batching is not configured here: the daemon flushes an accumulating batch to
# the durable queue when it reaches 500 events, 1 MiB of encoded events, or
# after 250ms of linger, whichever comes first. When the queue reaches
# state.max_queue_bytes the daemon stops reading inputs (backpressure to the
# source files, which persist) rather than dropping data.

logging:
  level: info
  format: json

server:
  # Set this to the server's collector gRPC listener. The loopback example
  # intentionally uses plaintext; a remote deployment must enable TLS below.
  # Placeholder names are chosen by this YAML document; the collector does not
  # automatically interpret an OPEN_SPLUNK_* environment namespace.
  address: "${OPEN_SPLUNK_COLLECTOR_SERVER_ADDRESS}"
  transport: grpc
  token_file: "${OPEN_SPLUNK_COLLECTOR_TOKEN_FILE}"
  compression: gzip
  tls:
    enabled: false # Local development only.
    # DANGER: with tls.enabled=false the bearer token is sent in CLEARTEXT.
    # Plaintext is permitted only to a loopback address (127.0.0.0/8, ::1,
    # localhost). Sending it to any remote host is REJECTED at startup unless you
    # explicitly acknowledge the risk by setting allow_insecure_remote: true
    # (only ever appropriate behind a trusted TLS-terminating sidecar/mesh).
    # allow_insecure_remote: false

state:
  directory: "${OPEN_SPLUNK_COLLECTOR_STATE_DIRECTORY}"
  max_queue_bytes: 1GiB
  dead_letter_max_bytes: 64MiB
  dead_letter_max_backups: 4

inputs:
  - id: gradethis-backend
    type: file
    # GradeThis development currently writes ../../.logs.tmp/gradethis.log
    # relative to its be process, while its production profile writes
    # /var/log/gradethis/app.log. Set GRADETHIS_LOG_PATH to the resolved path
    # visible to this collector process; do not copy production logs into this
    # repository.
    include:
      - "${GRADETHIS_LOG_PATH}"
    exclude:
      - "*.gz"
    format: ndjson
    start_at: end
    # index is required (event routing). host defaults to the OS hostname when
    # omitted; source defaults to the input id and sourcetype to the format.
    index: gradethis
    source: gradethis-backend
    sourcetype: go:zap:json
    # Set this explicitly when the collector is a sidecar; otherwise its own
    # container hostname would be recorded instead of the application host.
    host: "${GRADETHIS_HOST}"
    # Static fields are attached to every event as trusted metadata. The special
    # key "service" populates the canonical LogEvent.service; all other keys
    # become typed string fields.
    fields:
      service: gradethis
      environment: "${GRADETHIS_ENVIRONMENT}"

# These exact names are applied in the ordered structured processor chain and
# by a durability sanitizer before that chain. The sanitizer covers
# raw/message/structured data and follows only top-level rename paths that
# actually execute for an event before WAL append, so processor order cannot
# rename around a configured confidentiality policy. There is no implicit
# sensitive-field list; add every field that this deployment must redact.
processors:
  - type: redact
    fields:
      - token
      - authorization
      - password
      - session_token
      - cookie
      - api_key
      - private_key
    replacement: "[REDACTED]"

name: open-splunk

services:
  server:
    image: "${OPEN_SPLUNK_DEPLOY_SERVER_IMAGE:?set OPEN_SPLUNK_DEPLOY_SERVER_IMAGE to an exact Open Splunk server image}"
    restart: unless-stopped
    init: true
    user: "65532:65532"
    read_only: true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    environment:
      TMPDIR: /tmp
      OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_LOG_LEVEL: "${OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_LOG_LEVEL:-info}"
      OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_LOG_FORMAT: "${OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_LOG_FORMAT:-json}"
      OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_HTTP_LISTEN_ADDRESS: 0.0.0.0:8080
      OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS: "${OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS:-localhost,127.0.0.1}"
      OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_HTTP_TRUST_X_FORWARDED_PROTO: "${OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_HTTP_TRUST_X_FORWARDED_PROTO:-false}"
      OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_CONTROL_DATABASE_FILE: /var/lib/open-splunk/state/private/open-splunk.db
      OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_MASTER_KEY_FILE: /var/lib/open-splunk/state/private/master.key
      OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_LOCK_FILE: /var/lib/open-splunk/lock/private/open-splunk-server-open_splunk.server.lock
      OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_EXPORT_ARTIFACT_DIRECTORY: /var/lib/open-splunk/exports/private
      OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_ALERT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL: "${OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_ALERT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL:-}"
      OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_ALERT_PRIVATE_WEBHOOK_HOSTS: "${OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_ALERT_PRIVATE_WEBHOOK_HOSTS:-}"
      OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_ADMINISTRATOR_TOKEN: "${OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_ADMINISTRATOR_TOKEN:?set OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_ADMINISTRATOR_TOKEN}"
      OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_CLICKHOUSE_ADDRESS: "${OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_CLICKHOUSE_ADDRESS:-per-clickhouse:9000}"
      OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_CLICKHOUSE_USERNAME: "${OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_CLICKHOUSE_USERNAME:-clickhouse}"
      OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD: "${OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD:?set OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD}"
      OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_HEC_ENABLED: "${OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_HEC_ENABLED:-false}"
    ports:
      # Workspace APIs trust the caller. Remote access needs an authenticated proxy.
      - target: 8080
        published: "${OPEN_SPLUNK_DEPLOY_HTTP_PORT:-8080}"
        host_ip: 127.0.0.1
        protocol: tcp
    volumes:
      - server-state:/var/lib/open-splunk/state
      - server-lock:/var/lib/open-splunk/lock
      - server-exports:/var/lib/open-splunk/exports
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp:rw,noexec,nosuid,nodev,mode=0700,uid=65532,gid=65532
    networks:
      - per-obs-network
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - /usr/local/bin/open-splunk-server
        - healthcheck
        - -url
        - http://127.0.0.1:8080/readyz
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20
      start_period: 30s
    stop_grace_period: 60s
    pids_limit: 512

volumes:
  server-state:
  server-lock:
  server-exports:

networks:
  per-obs-network:
    driver: bridge

name: open-splunk-recovery

x-server: &server
  image: "${OPEN_SPLUNK_DEPLOY_SERVER_IMAGE:?set an exact server image}"
  user: "65532:65532"
  read_only: true
  cap_drop: [ALL]
  security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true]
  environment: &environment
    TMPDIR: /tmp
    OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_CONTROL_DATABASE_FILE: /var/lib/open-splunk/state/private/open-splunk.db
    OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_MASTER_KEY_FILE: /var/lib/open-splunk/state/private/master.key
    OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_ADMINISTRATOR_TOKEN_FILE: /var/lib/open-splunk/state/private/administrator.token
    OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_LOCK_FILE: /var/lib/open-splunk/lock/private/open-splunk-server-open_splunk.server.lock
    OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_SEARCH_ARTIFACT_DIRECTORY: /var/lib/open-splunk/state/private/search-artifacts
    OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_CLICKHOUSE_ADDRESS: clickhouse:9440
    OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_CLICKHOUSE_USERNAME: open_splunk_operator
    OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD_FILE: /run/recovery/operator.password
    OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_CLICKHOUSE_TLS_ENABLED: "true"
    OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_CLICKHOUSE_TLS_CA_CERTIFICATE_FILE: /run/recovery/ca.crt
    OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_CLICKHOUSE_TLS_SERVER_NAME: clickhouse
  volumes: &server-volumes
    - server-state:/var/lib/open-splunk/state
    - server-lock:/var/lib/open-splunk/lock
    - recovery-sets:/var/lib/open-splunk/recovery
    - recovery-archives:/var/lib/open-splunk-clickhouse-backups:ro
    - "${OPEN_SPLUNK_RECOVERY_CONFIG_DIRECTORY:?set absolute prepared recovery config directory}:/run/recovery:ro"
  tmpfs:
    - /tmp:rw,noexec,nosuid,nodev,mode=0700,uid=65532,gid=65532
  networks: [recovery]

services:
  server:
    <<: *server
    restart: unless-stopped
    init: true
    environment:
      <<: *environment
      OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_HTTP_LISTEN_ADDRESS: 0.0.0.0:8080
      OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS: "${OPEN_SPLUNK_SERVER_HTTP_ALLOWED_HOSTS:-localhost,127.0.0.1}"
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${OPEN_SPLUNK_DEPLOY_HTTP_PORT:-8080}:8080"
    stop_grace_period: 60s
    healthcheck:
      test: [CMD, /usr/local/bin/open-splunk-server, healthcheck, -url, "http://127.0.0.1:8080/readyz"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  recovery:
    <<: *server
    profiles: [tools]
    command: [help]

  prepare-recovery-volume:
    <<: *server
    profiles: [tools]
    user: "0:0"
    cap_add: [CHOWN, FOWNER, DAC_OVERRIDE]
    command: [prepare-clickhouse-recovery-volume, -path, /var/lib/open-splunk-clickhouse-backups, -log-path, /var/log/clickhouse-server]
    volumes:
      - recovery-archives:/var/lib/open-splunk-clickhouse-backups
      - clickhouse-logs:/var/log/clickhouse-server

  delete-recovery-archive:
    <<: *server
    profiles: [tools]
    user: "101:65532"
    command: [help, delete-deployment-recovery-archive]
    volumes:
      - recovery-archives:/var/lib/open-splunk-clickhouse-backups

  clickhouse:
    image: clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.7.5.10-alpine@sha256:0a45b864c73322d4360dea1973ee9b77f29c51af1242ad2d47409908071fa56e
    restart: unless-stopped
    user: "101:101"
    group_add: ["65532"]
    environment:
      CLICKHOUSE_SKIP_USER_SETUP: "1"
    volumes:
      - clickhouse-data:/var/lib/clickhouse
      - clickhouse-logs:/var/log/clickhouse-server
      - recovery-archives:/var/lib/open-splunk-clickhouse-backups

docker compose recovery topology

# production-shaped recovery topology; use instead of the plaintext default.
name: open-splunk-recovery

x-server: &server
  image: "${open_splunk_deploy_server_image:?set an exact server image}"
  user: "65532:65532"
  read_only: true
  cap_drop: [all]
  security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true]
  environment: &environment
    tmpdir: /tmp
    open_splunk_server_control_database_file: /var/lib/open-splunk/state/private/open-splunk.db
    open_splunk_server_master_key_file: /var/lib/open-splunk/state/private/master.key
    open_splunk_server_administrator_token_file: /var/lib/open-splunk/state/private/administrator.token
    open_splunk_server_lock_file: /var/lib/open-splunk/lock/private/open-splunk-server-open_splunk.server.lock
    open_splunk_server_search_artifact_directory: /var/lib/open-splunk/state/private/search-artifacts
    open_splunk_server_clickhouse_address: clickhouse:9440
    open_splunk_server_clickhouse_username: open_splunk_operator
    open_splunk_server_clickhouse_password_file: /run/recovery/operator.password
    open_splunk_server_clickhouse_tls_enabled: "true"
    open_splunk_server_clickhouse_tls_ca_certificate_file: /run/recovery/ca.crt
    open_splunk_server_clickhouse_tls_server_name: clickhouse
  volumes: &server-volumes
    - server-state:/var/lib/open-splunk/state
    - server-lock:/var/lib/open-splunk/lock
    - recovery-sets:/var/lib/open-splunk/recovery
    - recovery-archives:/var/lib/open-splunk-clickhouse-backups:ro
    - "${open_splunk_recovery_config_directory:?set absolute prepared recovery config directory}:/run/recovery:ro"
  tmpfs:
    - /tmp:rw,noexec,nosuid,nodev,mode=0700,uid=65532,gid=65532
  networks: [recovery]

services:
  server:
    <<: *server
    restart: unless-stopped
    init: true
    environment:
      <<: *environment
      open_splunk_server_http_listen_address: 0.0.0.0:8080
      open_splunk_server_http_allowed_hosts: "${open_splunk_server_http_allowed_hosts:-localhost,127.0.0.1}"
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:${open_splunk_deploy_http_port:-8080}:8080"
    stop_grace_period: 60s
    healthcheck:
      test: [cmd, /usr/local/bin/open-splunk-server, healthcheck, -url, "http://127.0.0.1:8080/readyz"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  recovery:
    <<: *server
    profiles: [tools]
    command: [help]

  prepare-recovery-volume:
    <<: *server
    profiles: [tools]
    user: "0:0"
    cap_add: [chown, fowner, dac_override]
    command: [prepare-clickhouse-recovery-volume, -path, /var/lib/open-splunk-clickhouse-backups, -log-path, /var/log/clickhouse-server]
    volumes:
      - recovery-archives:/var/lib/open-splunk-clickhouse-backups
      - clickhouse-logs:/var/log/clickhouse-server

  delete-recovery-archive:
    <<: *server
    profiles: [tools]
    user: "101:65532"
    command: [help, delete-deployment-recovery-archive]
    volumes:
      - recovery-archives:/var/lib/open-splunk-clickhouse-backups

  clickhouse:
    image: clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.7.5.10-alpine@sha256:0a45b864c73322d4360dea1973ee9b77f29c51af1242ad2d47409908071fa56e
    restart: unless-stopped
    user: "101:101"
    group_add: ["65532"]
    environment:
      clickhouse_skip_user_setup: "1"
    volumes:
      - clickhouse-data:/var/lib/clickhouse
      - clickhouse-logs:/var/log/clickhouse-server
      - recovery-archives:/var/lib/open-splunk-clickhouse-backups
      - ./recovery/clickhouse.xml:/etc/clickhouse-server/config.d/recovery.xml:ro
      - "${open_splunk_recovery_config_directory:?set absolute prepared recovery config directory}/users.xml:/etc/clickhouse-server/users.d/recovery.xml:ro"
      - "${open_splunk_recovery_config_directory:?set absolute prepared recovery config directory}:/run/recovery:ro"
    networks: [recovery]
    stop_grace_period: 60s

volumes:
  server-state:
  server-lock:
  recovery-sets:
  recovery-archives:
  clickhouse-data:
  clickhouse-logs:

networks:
  recovery:
